candidate.title: Webhook updates an arbitrary credential when user has multiple credentials for the same app
reports: credentials are matched only by userid and appid, so users with multiple accounts for one integration can have an arbitrary credential overwritten
app-credential.ts:65 identifies credentials only by user and app, so users with multiple credentials for one integration may have an arbitrary connected account overwritten
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 matches credentials only by userid and appid, so users with multiple accounts for one app may have an arbitrary credential overwritten

app-credential.ts:60-68 uses prisma.credential.findfirst({ where: { userid, appid } }), which picks an arbitrary row when a user has multiple credentials for the same app, silently overwriting the wrong account's tokens; the request schema has no disambiguator

in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, prisma.credential.findfirst({ where: { userid, appid } }) can pick an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple credentials for the same app, silently overwriting the wrong one, with no way in the payload to target a specific credential id

[bug] the webhook selects an arbitrary credential row via findfirst on {userid, appid} with no ordering and no way to target a specific credential, then overwrites its key. a user with multiple credentials for the same app (multiple connected accounts, which cal supports) has an unpredictable one overwritten by the parent app's push, silently destroying the other account's tokens; bookings on the clobbered account then fail with auth errors.
candidate.example: webhook's findfirst has no orderby, so it nondeterministically picks an arbitrary credential when duplicates exist
